extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and practitioners of American political parties and electoral/nomination procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and customary practices for party nominating conventions and party committees at ward, district, state, and national levels, including composition, timing, and functional responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of delegates by ward and town primaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Delegates to conventions are chosen in ward and town primaries; delegates from wards and primaries are elected at the same time with those for State, county, and councillor conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State convention and other nominating conventions draw delegates from ward and town primaries; timing is synchronized with other delegate elections.

rubrics_metrics.name: State central committee composition (senatorial-district representation and at-large additions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each senatorial district convention elects one member of the State central committee, and, among the Democrats, fifteen members at large are added to this central committee by the last preceding State convention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prescribes both district-based representation on the State central committee and (for Democrats, per the text) the practice of adding at-large members at the prior State convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: State convention composition and summons
rubrics_metrics.description: The State convention consists of delegates from ward and town primaries in proportion to their party votes at last elections, and is summoned by the State central committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State central committee is itself constituted of forty members elected in October by senatorial convention and takes office on 1st January; it issues the summons for the State convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: State central committee election timing and size
rubrics_metrics.description: The State central committee consists of forty members, elected in October by senatorial convention, and taking office on 1st January.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when and by whom the State central committee is chosen and the committee's fixed size (forty).

rubrics_metrics.name: State committee officers and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The State committee organizes by choice of chairman, secretary, treasurer, and executive committee, who oversee the whole State campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee elects its officers and an executive committee to manage and oversee statewide campaign activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: State convention nominates state executive candidates
rubrics_metrics.description: The State convention nominates the party candidates for governor, lieutenant-governor, secretary of state, treasurer, auditor, attorney-general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates the offices typically filled by nomination at the State convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: District conventions for Congressional nominations and call timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The convention in each district to nominate party candidates for the House is called every two years by a committee elected by the last convention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: District-level nominating conventions are periodic (biennial) and are convened by a committee chosen at the prior convention; delegates from wards and primaries participate and are elected contemporaneously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominating convention appointment of committee to call next convention (governor's council example)
rubrics_metrics.description: The convention for nominating members of the governor's council (eight in number) also appoints a committee to call the next convention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominating conventions may appoint a follow-up committee charged with summoning the subsequent convention (illustrated for governor's council nominations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation and selection of delegates to the National convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Every four years delegates to the National convention are chosen — under present party customs, two for each senator and representative of the State in Congress (e.g., Massachusetts then had thirty-two). Delegates corresponding to the representative districts are nominated by a convention in each district called in the spring; delegates corresponding to senators are chosen at a general convention in the spring called by the State central committee from wards and primaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies apportionment formula (two delegates per member of Congress) and dual nomination routes: district conventions for representative-corresponding delegates, and a general State convention for senator-corresponding delegates; the resulting State delegation then participates in selecting State members of the National committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: State selection of National committee members at National convention
rubrics_metrics.description: The thirty-two delegates at the meeting of the National convention choose the State members of the National committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State delegations at the National convention vote to elect that State's representatives to the party's National committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: National committee composition and method of election
rubrics_metrics.description: The National committee is elected one member by the delegates of each State at the last National convention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each State's delegation to the prior National convention selects one member to represent that State on the National committee; the National committee in turn calls the next National convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convention autonomy to make rules for procedure and election
rubrics_metrics.description: The National convention (and this is true in general of all conventions) may make rules for its own procedure and election — as, for example, that all State delegates shall be chosen at large instead of by districts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conventions have self-governing authority to set procedural rules and to alter delegate-selection methods (e.g., switching between district-based and at-large selection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation fairness / malapportionment concern at National conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaint that parts of the country in which there are very few members of the party have yet an undue share of representation in the conventions; no successful plan has yet been devised for overcoming the difficulty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies a recurring problem in delegate apportionment at National conventions: disproportionate representation of areas with low party membership and the lack of an agreed fix.

rubrics_metrics.name: National committee functions in managing the party campaign
rubrics_metrics.description: The National committee manages the party campaign, sending money and speakers to the weaker States, issues documents, collects subscriptions, and dispenses general advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarizes operational roles of the National committee: fundraising, resource allocation, communications, and advisory coordination across States.
